chunks: Saʿd narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī Naṣr, from ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn ʿAmr, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Ḥammād, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: I become heedless regarding the recitation in the first rakʿah. He said: Recite in the second. I said: I become heedless in the second. He said: Recite in the third. I said: I become heedless in my entire salat (prayer). He said: If you have preserved the rukuʿ and the sujud, then your salat (prayer) is complete.

His statement عليه السلام, 'If it escaped you in the first, then recite in the second,' did not mean that he should repeat the recitation that he missed in the first; rather, he meant that he should recite in the second and the third what pertains to each of them from the recitation. As for the first, its ruling has already passed. The correct understanding of that is that whoever forgets the recitation in the first two rakʿahs must recite in the third and fourth and leave the tasbih that would have been permissible for him had he recited in the first two, so that his salat (prayer) does not remain entirely without recitation.

key_terms.التَّسْبِيحَ: the glorification formula recited in later rakʿahs in place of recitation in some cases

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they forget the recitation in the first or second rakʿah of salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of one who forgets the recitation during salat (prayer), clarifying how he should proceed in later rakʿahs. It indicates that the prayer remains valid if the essential acts of rukuʿ and sujud are preserved, and it further explains that one who missed recitation in the first two rakʿahs should recite in the later rakʿahs instead of substituting tasbih.
